annotations.annotation_text: Page 89 opens Book 1, Chapter 4 ("The Burial of HCE") during the Age of Gods (transition) phase. This passage continues the burial of the giant in the landscape, the archaeological mound, the Four Annalists surveying history, featuring HCE, Mamalujo, Kate the Slop. The nocturnal dream-narrative layers Dublin topography, world mythology, and linguistic alchemy into polysemic prose.

annotations.annotation_text: Mid-page polysemic node on page 89 ("The Burial of HCE"): Joyce weaves multilingual puns across 60+ languages — etymological roots from the Contemporary Literature Press lexicons (Romanian, Scandinavian, Slavic, Classical) intersect with local Dublin speech rhythms. The Age of Gods (transition) dream-logic transforms ordinary syntax into a palimpsest of global literary and mythic references.
sources: Tindall, William York. A Reader's Guide to Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/readersguidetofi00tind
Contemporary Literature Press: Multilingual Lexicons for FW. https://editura.mttlc.ro

annotations.annotation_text: Fall/resurrection motif "ladder" on page 89 ("The Burial of HCE"): Tim Finnegan tumbling from his ladder, Humpty Dumpty shattering from the wall, Adam falling in Eden — all converge within the burial of the giant in the landscape, the archaeological mound, the Four Annalists surveying history. The comic-cosmic Fall during the Age of Gods (transition) phase demands its counterpart: resurrection through the whiskey-splash of the water of life (uisce beatha).
sources: The Ballad of Tim Finnegan's Wake. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finnegan%27s_Wake
